title: Do PCAOB Inspections Improve the Quality of Internal Control Audits?

scopes.description: Complete author-documented Stata preparation and analysis workflow embedded in master_prog.docx. It includes Tables 1–9 and random/fixed-effects variants, but requires extraction to a standalone driver and local input-path setup.

requirements.description: The exact author PCAOB inspection input ICFR.csv, with auditorkey, report_no, no_reports, inspect_begin, inspect_end, inspect_year, pcaob_report, examined-audit and total-deficiency counts, ICFR deficiency counts/categories, and the 2010–2013 auditor indicator.

routes.description: The exact author ICFR.csv is supplied, readable, and its raw columns match the documented inspection/date/deficiency fields. The datasheet states 2005–2014 reports; the bounded one-row probe does not independently establish full coverage. Native Stata naming of the long service-organization column before the line-214 rename remains a separate import-compatibility issue.
expected_fields: Number of audits examined by inspectors
Number of audits that are found to have significant deficiencies

Materiality. Deficiencies in assessing materiality of internal control weaknesses or failing to evaluate severity of detected IC weaknesses (eg that individual immaterial misstatements could be material when considered in aggregate)
Accounts. Insufficient testing of controls relating to specific accounts or inappropriate reliance on controls relating to specific accounts or over-reliance on management reviews
IT. Failure to test electronic data processing general and application controls
other parties (work of others including service organizations)
Work of others. Using the work of others (e.g., component auditors, internal auditors, external pricing vendors, outsourced loan review function)

Service organizastion. Failure to perform sufficient audit procedures to support the Firm's reliance on controls at service organizations. The issuer used an external service organization to service the enrollment of customers and to process transactions related to those customers, and data received from that service organization formed the basis for the issuer's recording of the majority of its revenue and accounts receivable, certain expenses, and the incurred-but-not-recorded ("IBNR") liability. The Firm failed to sufficiently test controls related to these accounts, as it failed to test the majority of the necessary user controls that the service auditor identified in its report on controls at the service organization.

Others (Failure to evaluate the period end financial reporting process; Failure to perform sufficient procedures to obtain an understanding of the issuer's design of internal controls; Failure to test budgetary controls; Failure to roll forward interim internal contorl procedures to the year-end date)
Period end. Failure to evaluate the period end financial reporting process
Understanding. Failure to perform sufficient procedures to obtain an understanding of the issuer's design of internal controls
Budgets. Failure to test budgetary controls.
triennially inspected auditors in the 2005-2007 period

issues.description: The packaged ICFR.csv contains the documented raw inspection and deficiency fields, but the document’s Stata code renames a service-organization field from liabilitythefirmfailedtosufficie (DOCX line 214). The native Stata name produced from the long CSV header has not been established. Keep the data route locally available; confirm the import name before relying on this rename.

The datasheet defines test_pct as a testing-deficiency measure, while the Table 5 code assigns test_pct=post_icfr_pct. The intended Table 5 variable and source are unresolved; do not infer a code repair.

The datasheet defines preins_pct as a binary adverse internal-control opinion in the preinspection window, while the program computes preins_icfr/presample, a deficiency share. Confirm the intended Table 8 definition and producer before changing the code.

Table 7 consumes future_restate, but no producer is visible in the supplied DOCX; the program merges misstate.dta without documenting whether it supplies that variable. Confirm the exact field/producer and company-fiscal-year mapping. This leaves full-pipeline closure incomplete.

The datasheet says the opinion and other-audit series include 2014, but the supplied program imports only 2004–2013. Whether 2014 is intentionally outside this program’s estimation scope or omitted from the supplied version is unresolved; do not append it or alter sample years without clarification.

The program is embedded in master_prog.docx and contains 133 hard-coded [redacted-path-86fcbbc8596e] path references across 53 input, intermediate, and output names. It requires extraction and consistent working-root setup before execution.

review_notes: The static audit reported no supported code or dependency edges, but the full DOCX program was manually traced. The DOCX contains the full Stata workflow; the assessment retains Tables 1–9 and the final random- and fixed-effects variants.

The supplied ICFR.csv is a verified local input for its documented raw fields. The one-row metadata probe does not establish complete coverage, and native Stata naming before the service-organization rename remains unresolved.
Current Compustat and Audit Analytics catalog hits are candidate routes only for the six other author datasets; no missing local license or access barrier is confirmed.

The preserved icfr_insheet_probe.log records Stata failing to find the self-written probes/icfr_insheet_probe.do file (r(601)); it does not test ICFR import compatibility or establish a runtime/license barrier.

The datasheet names opinion and other-audit files through 2014, while the supplied program imports 2004–2013 only. The 2014 scope is recorded for author clarification and was not appended to the sample.

The program uses [redacted-path-86fcbbc8596e] absolute Windows paths. Any future run setup must extract the embedded program to a working copy and keep input/intermediate/output roots consistent; no author source was edited or executed.
